Vertex models are a class of cell-based models developed to study tissues in which cell shapes can be approximated by polygons in two dimensions 21-25 or polyhedra in three dimensions 26.

Vertex models have been used to study a wide range of tissue phenomena, including a transition between solid-like and fluid-like states and various morphogenetic processes such as the polarization of early embryos, the formation of branched structures, and the biased elongation of tissues.
